items.title: Emile Christian and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-02-11
items.q: those days Johnny Detroit was around, he had his own style

ctx.x: Well, what about a guy that's like that? Ray Lopez down here. Would he play straight melody, or would he be a get-off man, or what? Well, he would be a...

Oh, oh, that's... It was in between. He had his own style. Emil had his own style, and, uh, those days Johnny Detroit was around, he had his own style, and Brunus had his own style. Everybody had their particular style.

See, because everybody's feeling is not the same. See, you feel one way, this fella's got a different interpretation. I have a different interpretation. You have, he has. We all have different interpretations. You see, we get so far, we can do so much. But the other fella, you'll hear, he plays the same as you do, but he's got little different things that he puts in. Well, you listen to him, say, that's good. He listen to you, he say, gee, that's nice. And, you know, this one takes this, this one takes that, you…
